You will join our Corporate Actions team. The team works with requirements and customer-facing activities related to corporate actions. The Business analyst role offers hands-on work with customer incidents, refinement of tasks and requirements, quality assurance, and user acceptance testing with customers. Your direct manager will be Ali Razvi.

**Primary tasks and responsibilities include:

**

• Respond to and follow up on incidents reported by customers.

• Analyze and drive refinement of requirements related to Corporate Actions

• Perform business gap & impact analysis and process mappings.

• Support quality assurance of the team’s solutions.

• Plan and conduct internal testing & user acceptance testing (UAT) with customers.

**To succeed you will have:

**

• A structured approach and an interest in working with documentation, notes, and detailed processes.

• Strong attention to detail.

• Experience with investments and markets.

• Danish language skills.

• Experience with ISO15022 & ISO 20022 protocols.

**It's nice-to-have:

**

• Experience with corporate actions and corporate actions event lifecycle.

• Jira, Confluence

**Be your best self with BEC's benefits!

**We offer a diverse range of benefits for our employees. Here are just a few of them.

• Professional development budget

• Healthy, varied lunch and fruit in the canteen

• Active staff associations: yoga, cycling, go-karting, games, bowling etc.

• Pension scheme

• Health and dentist insurance

• Referral bonus

**What does the recruitment process look like?

**

• Send us your CV: We want to get to know you

• Screening call: Let's chat and see if we're a match

• Meet your future manager and team: See who you'll be working closely with.

• Personality and cognitive test: Let's learn more about you.

• Meet our talent partner and your future manager once more: Get feedback on your test results.

• Time to sign the contract: We're ready to welcome you to BEC!

**If you have any questions about the position, please contact Anna Barcinska at Anna.Barcinska@bec.dk

**BEC is in the process of being acquired by our largest customer and co-owner, Nykredit, which is Denmark's largest mortgage provider and third-largest bank. We will become part of a new and larger organization called Nykredit Financial Technologies. In the transition phase, we are recruiting for roles that we expect to be highly needed in our future organization.

Who is Understory?

Understory is a vertical-focused software platform built for experience businesses – from kayaking tours to cooking classes. Our operating system helps creators manage operations, grow bookings, accept payments, and run their business with clarity and less stress.

We move fast, iterate quickly, and expect everyone to bring proactive solutions every day. You'll learn faster here than almost anywhere else because the challenges are real and the pace is high. This isn't about clocking in and out – the right candidate will get a lot of trust and ownership, and it's all about building something that matters to creators around the world.

We recently raised a €12M Series A and are scaling fast. With customers in 10+ countries and a growing presence internationally, our focus is global, our ambition is high, and our team is fully committed to being the go-to platform for experience creators worldwide.

In keeping with this momentum, we are growing our team across Copenhagen and Barcelona and doubling down on our Nordic markets.

About the Role

As our Nordic Account Executive, you'll be responsible for driving revenue growth in our Nordic markets from our Copenhagen or Barcelona office. You'll own the sales process from qualified opportunity to signed customer, helping experience providers discover how Understory can support and grow their businesses.

You'll work closely with SDRs, Customer Success, and Marketing teams to create a seamless customer journey while providing valuable market insights that help shape our growth strategy in the Nordics.

What You'll Do

• 
Own the full back end of the sales cycle for Danish, Swedish or Norwegian experience providers.

• 
Conduct product demonstrations and consultative sales conversations.

• 
Convert qualified leads into paying customers through effective negotiation and closing.

• 
Collaborate with SDRs to ensure smooth transitions from prospecting to opportunity management.

• 
Maintain accurate pipeline data and forecasting in CRM systems.

• 
Share insights from the Nordic markets to support product and commercial strategy.

• 
Represent Understory at relevant events and networking opportunities.

What Success Looks Like

Months 1–3 - Onboarding & Pipeline: Complete onboarding, build pipeline ownership, and confidently manage sales conversations.

Months 4–6 - Closing: Consistently close new customers and establish a healthy sales pipeline.

Months 7–12 - Revenue: Achieve or exceed revenue targets while contributing to Understory's long-term growth in the Nordics.

What We're Looking For

• 
You need to be native in one of our Nordic markets: native level of Danish, Swedish or Norwegian, plus fluency in English (written and spoken).

• 
2+ years of B2B sales experience, either as a top-performing SDR/BDR or as an Account Executive.

• 
Strong negotiation, presentation, and closing skills.

• 
A proactive and results-driven mindset with a passion for achieving goals.

• 
Passion for experiences, travel, and supporting entrepreneurs.

• 
Someone living in either Copenhagen or Barcelona to join one of our offices.

Nice to have:

• 
Experience within SaaS, hospitality, tourism, or experience-booking industries.

• 
Existing network within the Danish, Swedish or Norwegian tourism or events sector.

• 
Familiarity with CRM tools such as HubSpot, Salesforce, or Pipedrive.

• 
Experience working in a startup or scale-up environment.

• 
Additional European language capabilities.

Why You'll Thrive at Understory

• 
Be part of a high-growth company redefining the experience economy worldwide.

• 
Join Understory at a pivotal moment in our Nordic markets: as part of our growing Nordic team, you will help shape our regional strategy, local team culture, and market footprint.

• 
Work from our Copenhagen or Barcelona office while helping shape our growth in the Nordics.

• 
Enjoy autonomy, flexibility, and ownership in a fast-moving environment.

• 
Collaborate with ambitious colleagues who are passionate about building meaningful products.

• 
Benefit from significant opportunities for professional development and career progression.

Start Date & Application

If you're a high-achieving closer who is ready to take ownership of revenue growth and leave your mark as an Account Executive in the Nordics, we want to hear from you! Apply below to join us.

We review applications on a rolling basis and will hire as soon as we find the right person.

Start date: We're always on the lookout for great candidates, so don't hesitate to apply.

Factbird helps manufacturers improve performance with an AI-enabled, plug-and-play manufacturing intelligence suite. Real-time visibility on the shop floor. Connected operations. Data that actually turns into improvement, not just reports.

We’re expanding our Northern European sales team in Copenhagen and looking for a Business Development Representative to help us keep building momentum and opening doors in a market where we already have a solid presence. You’ll work from our Copenhagen office and support our Danish and Swedish markets, so we’re looking for someone fluent in both languages.

This is a great role for someone early in their sales career who wants more than a script to follow: someone who wants to help shape our outbound approach, sharpen their craft with modern prospecting tools, and sell something that makes a real difference on the factory floor.

About the Role

As a BDR at Factbird, you won’t just be executing outreach. You’ll be helping sharpen the playbook for how we generate pipeline in Denmark and Sweden. That means a mix of hands-on prospecting and real input into strategy: which accounts to target, which messages resonate, and which channels and tools actually move the needle.

You’ll spend your time identifying the right accounts, reaching the right people, testing what works, and turning interest into qualified meetings and sales opportunities.

This is a phone-first role. Phone calls remain your primary tool, but you’ll also run structured multi-channel campaigns across email and LinkedIn, and use AI-powered prospecting tools to work smarter, not just harder.

Key Responsibilities

We’re looking for someone who understands that outbound success comes from a combination of activity, discipline, messaging, and follow-through. This role is aligned with market expectations for outbound development work, including periods where 100-200 call attempts per day may be required, depending on territory focus, campaign goals, and lead quality.

What you'll do

• 
Build qualified pipeline through targeted outbound prospecting into manufacturing and industrial accounts across Denmark and Sweden

• 
Respond to inbound leads, qualify interest, and convert it into meetings

• 
Research target accounts to understand business context, likely pain points, and buying relevance

• 
Identify the right decision-makers and stakeholders within target organizations

• 
Book discovery meetings for the Account Management team and create qualified opportunities

• 
Maintain strong prospect data quality and keep HubSpot accurate and up to date

• 
Track your performance against KPIs and stay disciplined about activity and follow-up

• 
Work closely with the Account Management and Marketing teams to sharpen targeting, messaging, and handoff quality

• 
Bring insights from prospect conversations back to the team: what’s resonating, what isn’t

How we'll measure success

KPIs will be defined with your manager, but here's what we're tracking:

• 
Sales-qualified leads generated

• 
Discovery meetings booked and completed

• 
Conversion from leads to qualified opportunities

• 
Outreach volume, especially calls

• 
Inbound lead response time

• 
CRM discipline and data quality

This role is for someone who wants to see a direct line between their daily work, the strategies they help build, and commercial growth.

About you

You want to build a career in sales, and you’re ready for a role where you get real ownership, not just a list of calls to make. You’re comfortable in an outbound environment, curious about tools and experimentation, and motivated by the opportunity to improve fast. We’re looking for someone with:

• 
1-3 years of experience as an SDR in a B2B SaaS environment

• 
Fluency in Danish and Swedish, and strong English

• 
A strong interest in pipeline generation and outbound prospecting

• 
Comfort working in a phone-first sales development role

• 
The ability to succeed in a high-activity environment, including periods of 100-200 calls per day

• 
Curiosity about the manufacturing world and interest in learning how manufacturers operate

• 
Strong follow-through and personal ownership

• 
Experience working in a CRM, ideally HubSpot

• 
Hunger for a long-term career in sales

If you’re excited by building pipelines, learning fast, and helping bring modern software into manufacturing environments, we’d love to hear from you.

Why Factbird?

People are at the heart of everything we build. We believe great products come from empowered teams — and we work hard to create an environment where you can do your best work and have space for life beyond it.

• 
Flexible working hours — we trust you to manage your time

• 
Competitive salary — compensation that reflects your skills, experience, and impact

• 
Internet reimbursement — stay connected wherever you choose to work from

• 
Thoughtful, human onboarding — step-by-step support from day one

• 
Individual Development Plan conversations — bi-yearly career development aligned to your ambitions

• 
Company-wide kickoffs & team days — we come together regularly across teams and regions

• 
A global, inclusive culture — diverse backgrounds and perspectives, actively celebrated

Join Us

If this role feels like a match, we’d be excited to hear from you and explore how you could help shape the future of data collection and production monitoring at Factbird.

And if someone in your network comes to mind who might be a great fit, feel free to share this opportunity with them.

Please note that applications will be reviewed after November 20th.

At Factbird, we believe that great work starts with people feeling respected, valued, and included. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to building a workplace where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.

All employment decisions at Factbird are made based on business needs, role requirements, and individual qualifications, without discrimination based on gender, gender identity or expression, age, disability, marital or family status, nationality, ethnic or social origin, religion or belief, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected under applicable European and local employment laws.

We celebrate diversity in all its forms and believe that different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences make our teams stronger and our work better. We warmly encourage all qualified candidates to apply and to bring their whole selves to Factbird.

For more information or questions please contact us at khma@factbird.com

**Business Consultant - AECO Technical Advisory

****Position Overview

**Autodesk Consulting is looking for a Business Consultant to join our Northern Europe team. This remote role supports strategic customers across the region.

This is a senior individual contributor role combining business consulting, AECO industry expertise and executive advisory. You’ll work with some of Autodesk’s largest customers to shape transformation strategies, define target operating models, and develop business cases and roadmaps that deliver measurable business outcomes.

You’ll advise senior leaders, structure complex business challenges and lead strategic advisory engagements from discovery through executive decision-making. While you won’t configure or implement solutions, you’ll understand how Autodesk and complementary technologies fit within customers’ broader business and technology ecosystems, partnering with technical specialists to turn strategy into actionable delivery plans.

**Main Responsibilities

**

• Build trusted relationships with customer executives, business leaders and transformation teams, acting as a strategic advisor throughout the engagement

• Understand customer objectives, challenges and operating context to define outcome-driven transformation strategies

• Assess operating models, business processes, organizational capabilities, data and digital workflows to identify opportunities for improvement

• Define target-state operating models, transformation roadmaps, business cases, success measures and benefits realization plans

• Lead executive workshops, facilitate decision-making and align stakeholders across complex organizations

• Advise customers on how Autodesk and complementary AECO technologies support business outcomes through effective workflows, data management and interoperability

• Identify and prioritize opportunities for data, automation and AI based on business value, organizational readiness, governance and adoption

• Partner with Solution Architects, technical consultants and customer-facing teams to shape advisory engagements, validate strategic recommendations and develop credible delivery roadmaps

**Minimum Qualifications

**

• Substantial experience in AECO, management consulting or business transformation, with a proven track record of independently leading complex strategy and transformation engagements

• Deep expertise in at least one of the following: construction, infrastructure, engineering consultancy, utilities, or a closely related project-based, asset-intensive industry

• Strong working knowledge of Autodesk technologies or comparable AECO tool ecosystems, with the ability to discuss capabilities, workflow fit, data, interoperability and business value. Hands-on implementation expertise is not required

• Strong understanding of operating models, organizational change, governance, business cases and benefits realization

• Practical understanding of data-centric workflows, enterprise systems, automation, responsible AI and technology adoption

• Ability to lead through influence across cross-functional and international teams, with excellent communication and executive presentation skills

• Fluent English is required. Dutch and other European languages are highly valued

• Willingness to travel to customer meetings and Autodesk events across Northern Europe (up to 50%)

• Proven experience advising executives, structuring complex problems, facilitating high-stakes workshops and driving decisions

****Learn More

******About Autodesk

**Welcome to Autodesk! Amazing things are created every day with our software – from the greenest buildings and cleanest cars to the smartest factories and biggest hit movies. We help innovators turn their ideas into reality, transforming not only how things are made, but what can be made.

We take great pride in our culture here at Autodesk – it’s at the core of everything we do. Our culture guides the way we work and treat each other, informs how we connect with customers and partners, and defines how we show up in the world.

When you’re an Autodesker, you can do meaningful work that helps build a better world designed and made for all. Ready to shape the world and your future? Join us!

**Salary transparency

**Salary is one part of Autodesk’s competitive compensation package. For Netherlands based roles, we expect a starting base salary between 69,000 EUR and 101,200 EUR Annual. Offers are based on the candidate’s experience and geographic location, and may exceed this range. In addition to base salaries, our compensation package may include annual cash bonuses, commissions for sales roles, stock grants, and a comprehensive benefits package.

**Sales Careers

**Working in sales at Autodesk allows you to build meaningful relationships with customers while growing your career. Join us and help make a better, more sustainable world. Learn more here: https://www.autodesk.com/careers/sales

**Belonging

**We take pride in cultivating a culture of belonging where everyone can thrive. Learn more here: **https://www.autodesk.com/company/global-belonging

****In-Person Onboarding and Identity Verification

**This role may require in-person onboarding and/or in-person ID verification.

Do you want to be a valued part of the critical infrastructure that serves communities across Europe and beyond? Are you looking for an opportunity where you can make an impact, shape decisions, and accelerate your career?

If so, we are looking for dedicated, curious, and highly motivated graduates to join the DFDS Graduate Programme starting in September 2027.

**Be part of the movement - and play your part

**About The Role The DFDS Graduate Programme is a two-year fast-track programme for recent graduates with an interest in and passion for the maritime industry.

During the programme, you will complete three rotations across different areas of our Ferry Division. You will begin at our headquarters in Copenhagen, followed by a mandatory international rotation at one of our European hubs. Your final rotation at our headquarters will be tailored to your skills, interests, and our business needs.

Throughout the programme, you will gain broad exposure to both the operational and commercial sides of our Ferry Division while building valuable industry knowledge and professional experience.

Ferry Operations offers broad end-to-end exposure with sustainability, standardisation, and digitalisation at the heart of everything we do.

**Examples Of Interesting Tasks Could Be To:

**

• Help design and develop the vessels of tomorrow, supporting our green transition through electrification, ammonia, and green methanol initiatives.

• Support the operation and maintenance of our fleet of more than 70 RoRo, RoPax, and passenger vessels, covering everything from dry dock planning to crisis management and contingency handling.

• Contribute to our standardisation and digitalisation journey across eight owned terminals and more than 20 third-party terminals, where safety remains our highest priority.

• Support fleet planning, equipment optimisation, and our intercontinental rail setup, connecting ferry and logistics operations across our network.

In the commercial part of our Ferry Division, you will work alongside colleagues across Europe, supporting both B2B and B2C markets.

**Examples Of Interesting Tasks Could Be To:

**

• Support local and global sales teams and assist with key account management, ensuring our network is successfully marketed and sold across regions.

• Drive continuous improvement in customer service and booking processes through standardisation and digitalisation initiatives.

• Collaborate with IT teams to enhance and optimise our digital customer offerings.

• Work with operational teams to optimise routes and vessel capacity to meet customer demand.

• Support revenue management activities, including pricing optimisation and commercial performance analysis.

Across all rotations, you will work closely with highly skilled colleagues and engage with customers, suppliers, and partners throughout the maritime value chain. To support your development, each rotation will include both a dedicated manager and a mentor who will help you successfully navigate your learning journey.

Alongside hands-on experience at DFDS, you will participate in the Danish Shipping Education Programme, delivered by Danish Shipping. This programme consists of webinars, four seminars in Denmark, and one international seminar, covering key topics across the maritime industry.

****About You

****At DFDS, we believe the strongest teams are built on diversity, inclusion, and different perspectives. We are looking for candidates who:

• Have graduated from a relevant master’s degree by the start of the Graduate Programme in September 2027, preferably within maritime studies, supply chain, freight forwarding, logistics, sustainability, business, finance, engineering, or a related field.

• Have gained relevant experience through a student job, internship, exchange programme, or other extracurricular activities.

• Have no more than two years of full-time professional experience after completing your master's degree.

• Demonstrate strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

• Are collaborative team players who enjoy working with others and creating impact.

• Are curious, proactive, and eager to learn and develop professionally.

• Have an international mindset and are excited about working across cultures and locations.

Working at DFDS **Join the movement and grow with us

**As part of the DFDS Graduate Programme, you will become part of a strong graduate network across the company and build valuable connections across our international business. We offer a steep learning curve, meaningful responsibility from day one, and three interesting rotations designed to accelerate your professional development.

Are we a match? Apply now.  If your skills, experience, aspirations, and personality match this opportunity, we would love to hear from you.

Please Apply By Uploading Your CV no Later Than 30 November 2026. When Applying, You’re Also Asked To Answer The Following Questions:

• Why are you interested in joining the DFDS Graduate Programme?

• How will the programme help kickstart your career?

• How do you expect to contribute to the programme and DFDS?

• What do you believe will be your biggest challenge(s) during the programme?

**We look forward to hearing from you.

**Visit our Graduate site here to learn more and meet some of our people.

Join our Sitaware Extensions Program and help deliver customised integrations and extensions to Systematic's defence product suite, from sensor interfaces to radio drivers. As Senior Software Developer, you will combine software design, implementation and testing in a close-knit team working in an exciting domain.

The job

You will contribute to the delivery of high-quality integrations and extensions, from requirements analysis through software design, implementation and testing. Beyond hands-on development, you will help apply and improve our development process, and share your knowledge to support the team's growth.

In short, you can look forward to:

• Designing, implementing, documenting and debugging features, working primarily on back-end development (Java) and occasionally on front-end development (Angular)

• Analysing requirements, breaking them into technical tasks, and clarifying acceptance criteria

• Implementing and troubleshooting interfaces to hardware and external systems, such as sensors and radio interfaces

• Developing and maintaining unit and integration tests, and designing for testability

• Identifying issues and recommending improvements to code, tooling, pipelines and processes

Joining the team

You will be part of the Product Extension Team of around seven developers, test engineers and architects, part of the Sitaware Extensions Program within Defence Services. The team delivers customised integrations and extensions to Systematic's defence product suite, focusing on software- and hardware-related integrations such as sensor interfaces, radio drivers and interoperability with external systems, and continuously improves its own testing and development practices, methods and tools. This is a newly created position, so you will have real scope to shape how the role develops as the team continues to grow.

Your qualifications

To succeed in this role, you bring several years of software development experience gained in a structured, team-based environment, along with:

• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Software Technology or similar

• Hands-on experience with Java (or a related object-oriented technology) for backend development, and Angular (or a similar modern framework) for frontend development

• Fluent English; Danish is a nice-to-have

Alongside this, we value:

• Strong analytical abilities, with a focused and open mindset

• The ability to communicate intent and purpose clearly, both in writing and conversation

• Enjoys collaborating closely within a cross-functional team

Onboarding includes two three-day stays in Aarhus, and you should expect occasional travel of around two to ten days a year, mostly within Europe. Some onsite hardware testing may also be required, depending on integration needs.

Please note that you must be able to present a clean criminal record and have lived in a NATO and/or an EU country for the past seven years as we work with security-classified projects. Read more here.

Never stop developing

Start your development here

We will be assessing applications on an ongoing basis as we wish to welcome our new colleague as soon as possible, so click Apply Now and send us your CV today. If you have any questions, you are always welcome to contact us on tel. +45 8943 2000 and ask for Andreas Markussen, Senior Manager.

**💰 🇩🇰 up to 46,000 DKK gross/month (depending on seniority level)

**Intro

Monta powers the EV charging ecosystem. With 300,000+ monthly users and millions of charge sessions every month, our platform accelerates the electrification of mobility.

This is a fast-moving place. The problems are hard, the pace is quick, and the bar is high. If you like real ownership, figuring things out, and seeing the direct impact of your work, you’ll do well with us.

AI is built into how we work. It helps us ship faster, make better decisions, and stay lean. Everyone at Monta is expected to use AI tools thoughtfully - and to find smart ways to use them to move the work forward.

Our principles keep us grounded: Build Together & Finish, Sweat the Details, Customer First, and Aim for the Moon.

The best part of Monta is the people - sharp, ambitious, and good to be around. You’ll be challenged, supported, and trusted to deliver.

We’re looking for a Jun/Mid Level Engineer who’s ready to roll up their sleeves, take ownership, and build with us - through the grind and the wins.

This Is What You Will Achieve

• Owned an OCPP hardening project - chased down a recurring class of vendor quirks (malformed messages, connection drops, the long tail of hardware oddities), shipped the fix, and measurably cut failed sessions or disconnections for that device family.

• Helped shift the team from reacting to incidents to preventing them, through alerting and observability work that catches problems earlier.

• Made real progress on OCPP 1.6, OCPP 2.0.1, and OCPI standards work that other services and front-ends across Monta now rely on.

What You Will Do

• Build and maintain backend services in NetOps' OCPP and charge point domain - protocol handling, message processing, device state, integrations with hardware vendors.

• Debug things that only break in the field. A charge point in Belgium disconnects every 40 minutes - you'll read the OCPP traffic, reproduce it against our emulator, find the cause, and fix it.

• Improve observability and alerting. Add the metrics, dashboards, and alerts that mean the next person doesn't have to guess.

• Take part in on-call once you're ramped up, with a team that treats a rough night as a reason to fix the system, not a rite of passage.

• Automate manual work away - a meaningful part of NetOps' job is removing the human steps that don't scale as our network grows.

• Collaborate across Product, Support, and the operations teams who live with the consequences of what we ship. You won't work in a silo.

**A Brief Overview Of Our Tech Stack

**

• Kotlin services (JVM), with Java where it already lives

• PHP/Laravel monolith - parts of our charge point domain still run here

• OCPP 1.6 / 2.0.1 and OCPI protocol handling

• Event-driven work with Kafka where message volume calls for it

• Observability via Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenSearch/Kibana

• AWS + Kubernetes, with Terraform for infrastructure

What We’re Looking For

• 1–4 years of backend engineering experience, or a strong junior track record with real production exposure. You write clean, readable code and finish what you start.

• Comfortable in a JVM language - Kotlin preferred, Java fine, and we'll help you get there from another stack if the fundamentals are strong. Willingness to touch PHP in our legacy monolith when the work calls for it.

• You enjoy debugging, genuinely - logs, traces, packet-level detail, weird one-off reports from a single customer.

• A sense of ownership - you follow your work into production, watch it, and flag problems early rather than waiting to be asked.

• Nice to have: curiosity about the physical world (our systems talk to metal boxes with electricity in them); clear communication - you can explain what broke and why to someone who isn't an engineer; advanced, deliberate use of AI tools in your daily engineering workflow.

• Bonus points for: exposure to OCPP, OCPI, EV charging, or the EV industry as a driver or enthusiast; IoT, embedded, or telemetry systems where devices in the field misbehave; event-driven architectures (Kafka) or high-volume message processing; reliability/monitoring/on-call experience (Prometheus, Grafana, SLOs); Kubernetes, Terraform, or infrastructure-as-code exposure.

**If the mission excites you but your experience isn’t a perfect 1:1 match, apply anyway - we care about potential, not perfection.

**AI Competency

• You’ll be expected to work with AI-powered tools. Some we use:

• GitHub Copilot / Claude Code

• ChatGPT / Gemini / Claude

• Notion AI (docs, knowledge, meeting notes)

• Analytics & ML: Langfuse, PyTorch, Mastra

• AI-enhanced testing & monitoring (e.g., generative QA, Grafana ML)

• We don’t expect mastery of all - but we expect comfort learning, experimenting, and adopting AI responsibly.

Why Monta

• Impact, not easy mode - your work matters, and you’ll feel it every day.

• Ownership from day one - we don’t micromanage, we expect you to deliver.

• The grind is real - priorities shift, and flexibility is sometimes needed to get things across the finish line. But so are the rewards: impact, growth, and a team that has your back.

• The people are extraordinary - talented, driven, and fun to work with. You’ll be challenged, supported, and inspired in equal measure.

What We Offer

• A yearly education budget and extra days off to use it.

At Acodyne, you will help develop the software, high-power electronics, and robotic systems that bring our next generation of high-speed, heavy-lift cargo UAS to life, moving between code, schematics, the lab bench, and real flight hardware.

jobs.occupation: Women’s Academy 2027: Insights into the financial sector
jobs.description:
Step inside the world of finance and explore what happens on a busy trading floor, how major companies are financed and how a bank manages risk in changing markets and society. Women’s Academy is an 8-week student programme at Danske Bank’s headquarters, designed to give you first-hand insight into Large Corporates & Institutions and Group Risk & Compliance.

What you will be doing

Across eight weekly sessions, you will meet specialists from across Danske Bank who will introduce you to their work, share real perspectives from the industry and involve you in relevant business topics.

During the programme, you will:

• 
Explore areas such as Corporate Banking, Markets, Corporate Finance, Risk and Compliance

• 
Gain insight into how different parts of Danske Bank work together

• 
Work with practical topics linked to finance, risk and business decisions

• 
Hear directly from people working in the financial sector

• 
Meet other students who are curious about finance

• 
Become part of the Women’s Academy community

• 
Take part in a celebratory dinner at the end of the programme

• 
Receive a certificate of participation upon completing the Academy

The Academy was created to encourage more women to explore finance. Women are still underrepresented in several parts of the sector, and by opening our doors, sharing knowledge and providing access to role models, we want to make finance feel more accessible to a broader range of students.

About you

We welcome applications from university students between the second year of their bachelor’s degree and the second year of their master’s degree.

You do not need previous experience in banking or finance. You also do not need to know whether finance is the right career path for you yet. The Academy is a place to explore the sector from within and discover what captures your interest.

We are looking for students who:

• 
Are curious about finance, business, markets or risk

• 
Want to learn more about career opportunities in the financial sector

• 
Are motivated to take an active part in discussions and sessions

• 
Bring an open mindset and a willingness to explore new topics

• 
Come from any academic background and are interested in learning from others

Practical information

• 
Programme period: 8 weeks in Q1 2027

• 
Duration: Eight weekly sessions of approximately three hours

• 
Location: Danske Bank headquarters, Copenhagen

• 
Application window: 2 November-23 November

• 
Attendance: Participants are expected to attend all eight sessions

What we offer you

You will get a unique opportunity to experience the financial sector from the inside, meet specialists from across Danske Bank and build your understanding of how finance connects to companies, markets and society. You will also become part of a student community and gain access to people who can share their experiences, career paths and advice.

Are you ready to explore finance?

To apply, please submit your CV and answer five short questions about your motivation, what makes you curious about finance and what you hope to gain from Women’s Academy. Instead of submitting a cover letter, we would like to get to know your perspective through your answers. There are no right or wrong answers, and previous experience in banking or finance is not required. We encourage you to respond openly and honestly, drawing on the experiences that are meaningful to you, whether they come from your studies, work, interests or personal life.

• 
Tell us briefly about yourself and what currently interests you.

Maximum 100 words

• 
What motivated you to apply for Women’s Academy, and what makes you curious about the financial sector?

Maximum 150 words

• 
Tell us about something you have achieved that you are proud of. Why is it meaningful to you?

This can come from your studies, work, volunteering, hobbies or personal life. Maximum 150 words.

• 
What motivates or drives you when learning something new?

Maximum 100 words

• 
What do you hope to gain from Women’s Academy, and how would you contribute to the programme?

Maximum 150 words

For further information please contact:

• 
Victoria Witzeling, DEI Lead LC&I and BC, at viwi@danskebank.dk or +45 20 65 21 34

• 
Magnus Ulstrup, DEI Lead & Senior Transformation Consultant, Group Risk & Compliance, at magnus@danskebank.dk or +45 30 11 83 65

• 
Filippa Kjær, DEI Lead Student, at fkja@danskebank.dk

Join Danske Bank’s Women’s Academy and take your first step into the world of finance. We look forward to hearing from you!

Do you want to join a global leader in renewable energy infrastructure? If so, CIP Fund Solutions (CIP FS) is looking for an Analyst to join our office in Copenhagen, Denmark.

Team

You will join a dynamic and collaborative finance team working across multiple international entities. The team consists of Financial Controllers based in London, Sheffield, Madrid, and Copenhagen, creating a diverse and international working environment. The role is based in our Copenhagen office, and you will work closely with and report to the Copenhagen based team.

We are responsible for financial reporting, accounting, and compliance for a broad portfolio of companies, and we collaborate closely with both internal stakeholders and external advisors across EMEA region. The team values accuracy, ownership, and clear communication, while maintaining a supportive and informal culture where collaboration and continuous learning are key.

Role

You will become an integral part of our expanding team in Accounting, Compliance, and Controlling team for EMEA. We are committed to supporting your professional development and providing valuable learning opportunities.

The role offers broad exposure to finance, accounting, compliance, and corporate administration across a portfolio of international renewable energy investments. You will support the Financial Controllers with recurring accounting and controlling activities, while also assisting with KYC processes, banking documentation, and other corporate and regulatory requirements applicable to our entities.

You will work closely with internal stakeholders, banks, auditors, legal advisers, corporate service providers, and other external counterparties. Through this combination of responsibilities, you will gain practical experience in how international investment structures are established, financed, administered, and maintained throughout their lifecycle.

Responsibilities will consist of but are not limited to:

• Supporting recurring accounting and controlling activities, including cost controlling, balance-sheet controlling, reconciliations, and monitoring of equity contributions

• Reviewing and processing financial information, internal reports, annual reports, and tax-related documentation

• Assisting with KYC and due-diligence requests from banks, auditors, etc.

• Supporting the opening, maintenance, and closure of bank accounts, including the preparation and coordination of required forms, supporting documentation, signatures, and internal approvals

• Assisting with bank-access administration and the maintenance of authorized users and signatories

You

You are a final-year BSc or first-year MSc student in Finance, Economics, Business, Accounting, Auditing, Business Law, or another relevant field. You are motivated by transforming theory into practical solutions and are interested in gaining broad experience across finance, accounting, banking, compliance, and corporate administration.

You enjoy working with both numbers and documentation and are comfortable coordinating tasks involving several stakeholders. You work in an organized way, pay close attention to detail, and see tasks through to completion.

We look for the following in a candidate:

• Structured problem-solving skills and a responsible approach to tasks

• Close attention to detail and a high level of accuracy

• An interest in operational finance, accounting, compliance

• Ability to follow up effectively with internal and external stakeholders

• Proficiency in English, both in writing and speaking, paired with effective communication skills

• Previous experience within finance, accounting, banking, compliance, legal administration, or a similar area is beneficial but not a requirement.

The process

Please apply online as soon as possible as applications will be processed on an ongoing basis. For questions related to the role, please reach out to our Talent Acquisition team at recruitment@cipfs.com. We do not include CV's and Cover Letters sent by email.

As we continue to improve our candidate experience, diversity and avoid unconscious bias, please avoid having a photo in your CV. We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality for all applicants.

Please be aware that we will not accept speculative CV submissions for any of our roles from recruitment agencies, and any unsolicited candidate submissions will be exempt from any payment expectations and ownership.

---

CIP Fund Solutions’ commitment to diversity and inclusion

CIP Fund Solutions is committed to securing a diverse and inclusive work environment where everyone feels respected and heard.

A diverse workforce allows CIP Fund Solutions to achieve results through different approaches and solutions to task execution and problem solving. We want all our employees to have equal opportunities for personal growth and career opportunities regardless of age, gender, sexual orientation, disability, religion, nationality, or ethnicity.

CIP Fund Solutions

CIP FS’ purpose is to enable CIP’s ambition to scale rapidly over the coming strategy-period - supporting our colleagues with professional and efficient financial, legal, tax and business operations through the cycle from fund formation and capital raising, to deploying investments into construction of large-scale greenfield renewable energy assets, as well as M&A.

For more information, please visit CIP Fund Solutions.

jobs.occupation: Analyst in Capital Planning – Help Shape the Bank’s Financial Future
jobs.description:
Capital planning sits at the heart of how Danske Bank balances financial resilience with sustainable growth. As part of a close-knit analytical team, you will contribute to decisions that enable the bank to serve its customers and support its strategic ambitions. This is a role where your work genuinely matters and where you will build a solid foundation in capital management.

What you will be doing

The Capital Planning team is part of Financial Resource Management in Group Treasury, sitting within Danske Bank's CFO area. The team of seven works on capital target setting, capital issuances, dividend decisions and macroeconomic stress testing. Your analyses and reports will receive close attention from the Executive Leadership Team, the Board of Directors and financial regulators. The atmosphere is collaborative, with knowledge sharing and learning woven into everyday working life, and the team takes pride in delivering high-quality work while enjoying the process.

More specifically, you will:

• Support monthly capital and MREL assessments and projections

• Analyse the effects of regulatory and model changes with relevant teams

• Contribute to stress tests and assessments of capital targets and buffers

• Help analyse payout capacity and capital and MREL funding needs

• Prepare decision material and gradually take ownership of defined deliverables

About you

• Master's degree in economics, finance, business administration or a related field

• Strong analytical skills and a structured, detail-oriented approach

• Ability to communicate complex findings clearly in English

• Curious and collaborative, with an interest in learning and developing within the field

• Comfortable working independently on defined tasks while contributing to team goals

Experience in banking or capital management, and familiarity with Python, SQL or similar tools, would be a welcome addition. We consider candidates at different stages of their career, so we encourage you to apply whether you are just starting out or bring a few years of relevant experience.

What we offer you

You will join a dedicated team where collaboration and continuous learning are part of daily work. Strengthen operational governance and accountability across functions, value chains, business services, processes, manual services, SOPs and business procedures.

Create foundations for AI, automation and data-driven operations through high-quality operational information and strong design principles.

• 
Partner across the Bank, connecting business, operations, architecture, technology, data, risk, controls and transformation perspectives.

•

Proven leadership experience from leading large specialist or transformation teams with a broad range of deliverables.

• 
Strong expertise in business architecture, process management and/or operating model design.

• 
Strong business acumen and the ability to connect strategic objectives with operational realities.

•

Experience driving enterprise-wide change in a complex and regulated environment, preferably financial services.

About the role

As Head of Physical Security & Safety, you will be responsible for protecting Saxo's people, facilities, operations and reputation across multiple international locations.

You will lead the development of our physical security framework, drive risk-based security initiatives, strengthen preparedness and crisis response capabilities, and ensure that security remains aligned with the evolving threat landscape.

You will work closely with senior stakeholders, facility management, IT Security, Risk, Compliance, and international office representatives to ensure a consistent and robust security posture across the bank.

Your responsibilities

• 
Lead Saxo's physical security and safety programme across global locations.

• 
Identify, assess and mitigate threats and vulnerabilities affecting employees, facilities and business operations.

• 
Develop and implement security policies, standards and operating procedures.

• 
Drive incident management, investigations and corrective actions where required.

• 
Strengthen emergency preparedness, crisis response and resilience capabilities.

• 
Oversee physical security technologies including access control, CCTV and alarm systems.

• 
Provide strategic security advice to senior management and key stakeholders.

• 
Manage security service providers and external security partners.

• 
Promote a security-aware culture through training and awareness programmes.

• 
Support major events, critical incidents and business continuity initiatives.

Your profile

You may come from law enforcement, the military, intelligence services, critical infrastructure, corporate security or a similar environment where security, risk management and operational leadership have been central to your role.

We expect you to bring:

• Extensive experience within physical security, protective security or security operations.

• A strong understanding of threat assessment, risk management and incident response.

• Experience leading security programmes, projects or specialist teams.

• The ability to advise and influence senior stakeholders.

• A calm and structured approach in high-pressure situations.

• Strong personal integrity, sound judgement and discretion.

• Fluency in English and Danish.

We are looking for an experienced Senior Product Manager for the DK Pension to take responsibility for the ongoing management and development of Saxo’s Danish pension offering.

About the job

The role combines pension domain responsibility with senior product management. You will work with the regulatory, operational and commercial aspects of the pension offering, while also helping to drive the product roadmap and digital development.

You will collaborate across business, technology and control functions and play an important role in translating pension regulation, client needs and business requirements into product priorities and solutions.

Key responsibilities

DK Pension and domain management

• Take responsibility for the Danish pension offering and its ongoing development

• Maintain a strong understanding of Danish bank pension regulation, taxation and relevant market developments, and translate changes into business and product requirements

• Help ensure that the pension offering remains compliant and operationally sound in collaboration with Legal, Compliance, Tax and Operations

• Act as a pension subject-matter expert and point of contact across relevant parts of the organisation

• Support operational teams with pension-related processes, requirements and work instructions where needed

• Manage relationships with an external pension vendor as well as partners, including new requirements, changes and prioritisation

• Participate in external forums and working groups to keep current with market best practices and upcoming regulatory changes

Senior Product Management

• Own and develop the product vision and roadmap for the pension offering, balancing regulatory requirements, client needs and business priorities

• Work with the Head of Pension to manage and prioritise the development backlog based on business needs, client value, regulatory requirements and technical dependencies

• Translate pension, tax and regulatory requirements into clear product and development requirements

• Work closely with technology teams throughout development and implementation

• Coordinate across Technology, Onboarding, Operations, Legal, Compliance and other relevant stakeholders

• Contribute to the continued development of the digital pension customer journey, including opportunities to improve usability and self-service

• Follow initiatives from initial requirements through implementation and subsequent improvements

Your profile

We are looking for someone with practical knowledge of pensions and experience from the Danish financial sector who is comfortable working with both product development and regulatory requirements.

You may currently work within a pension company, bank, investment firm or another regulated financial institution.

We expect that you bring:

• Relevant professional experience from the Danish financial sector, with experience related to bank pension framework; ratepension, aldersopsparing and kapitalpension

• Good knowledge of Danish pension products and the regulatory and tax framework surrounding them

• Experience from a product-focused role, such as Product Owner, Product Manager, pension product specialist, business developer or a similar position

• Experience translating regulatory, business or operational requirements into product solutions

• Experience working with digital development and prioritising requirements or a product backlog

• Strong stakeholder management and communication skills

• A structured approach to prioritisation and the ability to work with regulatory, operational, commercial and client considerations simultaneously

• Fluent in Danish and English

Nice to have

• Experience with digital investment or trading platforms

• Knowledge of Aktiesparekonto (ASK) and the broader Danish investment and savings landscape

• Experience collaborating with external pension providers, administrators or technology vendors

• A member of external forums and established working groups with deep technical expertise & an industry-wide network

About you

You have a solid understanding of pensions and an interest in how pension products can be developed and improved through digital solutions.

You are comfortable working with different types of stakeholders, from Compliance and Legal to Operations and Technology, and can translate pension-related requirements into practical solutions.

The role could suit someone who has already worked as a Product Owner or Product Manager within pensions, but it could also be relevant for an experienced pension professional who has worked closely with digital product development.

You combine pension knowledge with a structured and collaborative approach and are comfortable taking responsibility for both the day-to-day product agenda and the longer-term development of the pension offering.

About the Role

As a Tax Services Product Specialist, you will help shape and develop Saxo’s global tax service offering, connecting tax expertise with investment products, custody infrastructure and technology.

You will design, improve and evolve processes across withholding tax, Relief at Source, tax reclaims, documentation, beneficial owner disclosure and financial transaction taxes, turning complex tax and market requirements into practical, scalable solutions.

Working across Tax Operations, Corporate Actions, Custody, Product, Technology, Compliance and Legal, you will translate regulatory and market developments into effective tax services, processes and controls. You will also collaborate with custodians, paying agents and tax service providers internationally.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys solving complex problems, connecting the dots across functions and turning specialist tax knowledge into better products and services.

Key areas of responsibility include:

• Define and maintain tax services, tax treatment rules, investor classifications and operational requirements, including eligibility, limitations and controls.

• Work with Operations, Product and Technology to enhance tax processes, system solutions and automation, and implement new tax and custody solutions.

• Support tax remittance processes covering withholding taxes, financial transaction taxes, stamp duties and other local tax requirements.

• Investigate tax-related incidents and client cases, identify root causes and drive remediation, process improvements and service documentation.

• Work with custodians, paying agents, tax vendors and other providers, while providing tax subject-matter expertise and supporting risk assessments, controls, audits and regulatory reviews.

Your profile

The role is suited to professionals with experience in investment tax, custody, securities services, corporate actions, asset servicing or related areas within financial services.

Relevant experience and knowledge may include:

• Experience in tax operations, custody, securities services, corporate actions or asset servicing.

• Knowledge of withholding tax and cross-border investment taxation.

• Experience with tax processes, documentation, Relief at Source, tax reclaims or beneficial owner disclosure.

• Ability to interpret tax guidance, regulatory requirements and market practices.

• Experience translating requirements into processes, controls or system solutions.

• Experience working with global custodians, intermediaries or service providers.

• Strong analytical skills and experience resolving tax or operational cases.

• Experience developing procedures, service documentation or control frameworks.

• Ability to communicate complex tax and operational topics to different stakeholders.

• Experience collaborating effectively across functions and with external partners.

Additional Relevant Experience

Experience in one or more of the following areas would be beneficial:

• Global custody models, including omnibus and segregated structures.

• Financial transaction taxes, stamp duties and other investment taxes.

• Regulatory or market change initiatives.

• Tax product or service development.

• Tax technology, automation or system implementation.

• Multi-market tax remittance and reporting.

• Service governance, operational risk or controls.

More about the role

The position provides the opportunity to work across international markets, tax regimes and custody networks and contribute to the ongoing development of Saxo’s tax service offering.

The role combines tax subject-matter knowledge with custody, operations, service development and technology. It therefore provides exposure to both the technical requirements associated with investment taxation and the operational and system solutions required to deliver tax services at scale.

_Do you want to join a global leader in renewable energy infrastructure? If so, CIP Fund Solutions (CIP FS) is looking for a Global Mobility Manager to join our office in Copenhagen, Denmark.

Team

You will join a global People team of more than 15 colleagues with diverse responsibilities and mandates. You will be part of the HR Legal & Mobility team, which comprises six colleagues.

Role

As Global Mobility Manager, you will manage global mobility cases and key operational workstreams across global tax, social security, immigration and relocation.

You will advise internal stakeholders on mobility processes, coordinate complex cross-border matters with specialist advisers, and ensure timely delivery in line with Mobility Policies and approval requirements.

Working closely with People, Payroll, Finance and external providers, you will identify risks early and lead improvements to mobility processes, systems and employee experience.

Responsibilities will include:

• Manage mobility cases end to end across global tax, social security, immigration and relocation, resolving complex issues.

• Oversee mobility compliance, documentation and data controls, including timely and accurate reporting of taxable vendor benefits.

• Advise stakeholders on mobility arrangements and policies, turning global specialist advice into action.

• Manage vendor performance, costs and escalations, including invoice review and internal cost recovery.

• Support stakeholder reporting on mobility progress, costs, risks and recommendations.

• Support mobility process improvements, including workflow optimization, integration and data management, and contribute to policy updates and implementation.

You

You have a relevant university degree and 5+ years of experience in global mobility within an international business or professional services firm.

You have experience managing cross-border mobility cases, coordinating tax, social security and immigration, and leading operational workstreams.

You are comfortable advising business stakeholders, managing external providers and exercising sound judgment on when to resolve matters independently and when to seek specialist input or escalate.

You also have a genuine interest in using AI and technology to improve service delivery and ways of working.

We look for the following in a candidate:

• Solid business acumen and ability to translate specialist advice into practical recommendations.

• Proven ability to own multiple cases and projects, coordinate contributors and resolve issues to deliver agreed outcomes.

• Sound judgment and initiative, with a structured, detail-oriented approach to prioritizing, anticipating dependencies and adapting to changing business needs.

• Experience optimizing mobility processes and implementing them within a mobility system is considered an advantage, but not a requirement.

• Fluency in English, both spoken and written.

The process

Please apply online as soon as possible as applications will be processed on an ongoing basis. For questions related to the role, please reach out to our Talent Acquisition team at recruitment@cipfs.com. We do not include CV's and Cover Letters sent by email.

As we continue to improve our candidate experience, diversity and avoid unconscious bias, please avoid having a photo in your CV. We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality for all applicants.

Please be aware that we will not accept speculative CV submissions for any of our roles from recruitment agencies, and any unsolicited candidate submissions will be exempt from any payment expectations and ownership.

CIP Fund Solutions is committed to securing a diverse and inclusive work environment where everyone feels respected and heard.
